p: Tintagel's link with King Arthur largely comes from the twelfth-century writer Geoffrey of Monmouth, who claimed Arthur was conceived here. The story stuck so well that Earl Richard is thought to have built his castle in the 1230s partly because of it, wanting a piece of that legendary glamour. So even the medieval ruins are, in a way, a product of the myth. The footbridge, opened in 2019, now carries you over the gap where the original land bridge once stood.
Allow at least two to three hours, more if you want to linger on the island or go down to the beach. Mornings and evenings are usually quieter than the middle of the day in summer.

Back on the clifftop, St Materiana's Church stands alone overlooking the sea, and it's a peaceful spot after the bustle of the castle. In the village, King Arthur's Great Halls leans into the legend with stained glass and storytelling. A short drive along the coast, Trebarwith Strand is a cracking beach at low tide, while Boscastle, with its pretty harbour and Museum of Witchcraft and Magic, makes a brilliant next stop. Rocky Valley, between the two, is lovely for a short walk.
